In [[algebra]], a '''primordial element''' is a particular kind of a [[Vector (mathematics and physics)|vector]] in a [[vector space]]. 

== Definition ==

Let <math>V</math> be a vector space over a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] <math>\mathbb{F}</math> and let <math>\left(e_i\right)_{i \in I}</math> be an [[Indexed family|<math>I</math>-indexed]] [[Basis (linear algebra)|basis]] of vectors for <math>V.</math> 
By the definition of a basis, every vector <math>v \in V</math> can be expressed uniquely as
<math display=block>v = \sum_{i \in I} a_i(v) e_i</math>
for some <math>I</math>-indexed family of scalars <math>\left(a_i\right)_{i \in I}</math> where all but finitely many <math>a_i</math> are zero. 
Let
<math display=block>I(v) = \left\{i \in I : a_i(v) \neq 0\right\}</math>
denote the set of all indices for which the expression of <math>v</math> has a nonzero coefficient. 
Given a subspace <math>W</math> of <math>V,</math> a nonzero vector <math>p \in W</math> is said to be {{em|primordial}} if it has both of the following two properties:<ref>Milne, J., [http://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/cft.html Class field theory course notes], updated March 23, 2013, Ch IV, §2.</ref>
#<math>I(p)</math> is minimal among the sets <math>I(w),</math> where <math>0 \neq w \in W,</math> and
#<math>a_i(p) = 1</math> for some index <math>i.</math>
